To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of dietary vitamin D3 on egg production and eggshell quality are not significant.
increasing dietary calcium to 3.4% increased percentage hatchability and decreased embryonic mortality in turkey hens, but dietary vitamin D3 had no significant effect.

increasing dietary calcium from 1.16 to 2.34 percent significantly improved body weight and feed conversion efficiency, egg production and hatchability, but that vitamin D3 in levels above established recommendations had no statistically significant beneficial effects on the parameters studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between dietary calcium and vitamin D3, and the reproductive characteristics of Small-type White turkey hen.
the effect of vitamin D and calcium on egg production, hatchability, and shell quality.
the effect of vitamin D3 and dietary calcium on the reproductive efficiency of turkey hens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimum dietary calcium level for egg production, egg weight, egg shell quality, and hatchablilty in the turkey hen is 2.25%.
the dietary requirements of the turkey hen are similar to the requirements of the domestic fowl.
the hen is a very poor indicator of vitamin D requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium and vitamin D3 are essential for normal egg production and eggshell quality in the turkey hen.
dietary calcium in excess of 1.16% and vitamin D3 in amounts exceeding the established requirement are not beneficial for the hen.
dietary calcium is more important than vitamin D3 in promoting reproductive efficiency in the turkey hen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin D is not a limiting factor in egg production or hatchability, and calcium is the key nutrient for these parameters.
calcium is the key nutrient to consider when trying to improve egg shell quality and hatchability.
calcium and vitamin D are essential for eggshell production, but that calcium is the limiting nutrient for shell production.
